records.c: Wellington initial object array for bit 7 marks an activated record, and bits 0 and 6 can keep it out of the activation scan at $297A. $41BE rebuilds it from the selected round record.
Wellington initial object array for world X values tested against window edges $2B and $2C at $299A and $299E. $41BE rebuilds it from the selected round record.
Wellington initial object array for world Y values tested against window edges $2D and $2E at $29A5 and $29A9. $41BE rebuilds it from the selected round record.
Wellington initial object array for fourth bytes copied into $1C at $29E4 and written back at $2A40. $41BE rebuilds it from the selected round record.
Wellington round 1 object records. The scan starts at index $13. The following 64 four-byte groups transpose into $9800, $9840, $9880 and $98C0 at $41EE.
Wellington round 2 object records. The scan starts at index $10. The following 64 four-byte groups transpose into $9800, $9840, $9880 and $98C0 at $41EE.
Wellington round 3 object records. The scan starts at index $1A. The following 64 four-byte groups transpose into $9800, $9840, $9880 and $98C0 at $41EE.
Wellington round 4 object records. The scan starts at index $20. The following 64 four-byte groups transpose into $9800, $9840, $9880 and $98C0 at $41EE.
Little-endian pointers to the four Wellington round object lists. $41D6 selects a pointer with twice the round number.
Wellington per-glyph attributes. The VIC color comes from the low nibble. Gameplay probes test the high bits at sites such as $0F34 and $0F3B.
Wellington map rows 0–7, numbered from the map origin. Each row is 128 metatile IDs. The column renderer at $2473 expands IDs through $5600/$5700.
Wellington map rows 8–15, numbered from the map origin. Each row is 128 metatile IDs. The column renderer at $2473 expands IDs through $5600/$5700.
Wellington map rows 16–23, numbered from the map origin. Each row is 128 metatile IDs. The column renderer at $2473 expands IDs through $5600/$5700.
Wellington map rows 24–31, numbered from the map origin. Each row is 128 metatile IDs. The column renderer at $2473 expands IDs through $5600/$5700.
Wellington definitions for metatiles $00–$3F. Each is a four-column set of four glyphs, indexed as four times the column plus the row at $24C0–$24F7.
Wellington definitions for metatiles $40–$7F. Each is a four-column set of four glyphs, indexed as four times the column plus the row at $24C0–$24F7.
Wellington definitions for metatiles $80–$BF. Each is a four-column set of four glyphs, indexed as four times the column plus the row at $24C0–$24F7.
Wellington definitions for metatiles $C0–$FF. Each is a four-column set of four glyphs, indexed as four times the column plus the row at $24C0–$24F7.
Wellington disk-loaded initial bytes for the first playfield matrix. The map column renderer writes its displayed rows beginning at $C0F0.
Wellington disk-loaded initial bytes for the second playfield matrix. The renderer pairs its $C4F0 output with $C0F0 in the first matrix.
Wellington playfield character graphics at the VIC bank-3 charset base. Each of its 256 screen codes selects eight bytes.
The Wellington upper glyphs include building edges and vertical bars, followed by repeated strips also visible in the Waitomo font.
